trials.output:
Reviewing the Windows DPAPI secret-persist path in Source_Core/src/ConfigManager.cpp.

Finding 1 (HIGH) — Source_Core/src/ConfigManager.cpp:374
j.erase("github_pat") runs unconditionally and is immediately followed by j["github_pat_enc"] = ProtectSecretForConfig(config.GitHubPat). If ProtectSecretForConfig fails and returns an empty string, the plaintext PAT has already been erased and the encrypted form is empty, so the only copy of the GitHub PAT is irrecoverably lost on the next write. Two lines below, the mcp_auth_token field demonstrates the correct guarded-erase pattern: it computes the encrypted value first, then only erases the plaintext when the token is empty OR the encryption succeeded (config.McpAuthToken.empty() || !mcpAuthTokenEnc.empty()). The github_pat (and token / plane_api_key) erases should adopt the same guard.

No other correctness or credential-safety issues found in this hunk.

findings.summary: j.erase(github_pat) runs unconditionally before its DPAPI encrypt is confirmed non-empty; if ProtectSecretForConfig fails the PAT is lost. mcp_auth_token below shows the correct guarded-erase.
